questions.question: Given below are four statements (a-d) regarding human blood circulatory system (i) Arteries are thick-walled and have narrow lumen as compared to veins (ii) Angina is acute chest pain when the blood circulation to the brain is reduced (iii) Persons with blood group A B can donate blood to any person with any blood group under A B O system (iv) Calcium ions play a very important role in blood clotting Which two of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Explanation: Statement (i) is correct: Arteries are thick-walled and have a narrow lumen compared to veins. This is because arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure from the heart to different body parts. Veins, on the other hand, are thin-walled, have a wider lumen, and carry deoxygenated blood at lower pressure. Statement (ii) is incorrect: Angina is chest pain that occurs due to reduced blood supply to the heart muscles, not the brain. A reduced blood supply to the brain causes a stroke, not angina. Statement (iii) is incorrect: Persons with blood group AB are universal recipients, meaning they can receive blood from any group. However, they cannot donate to all blood groups. They can only donate to AB recipients. Statement (iv) is correct: Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) play an important role in blood clotting. They help convert prothrombin into thrombin, which is necessary for clot formation. Thus, the correct answer is A) (i) & (iv).

questions.question: Identify A, B and C in the given diagram. Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: To identify A, B, and C, we need to analyze their structural characteristics: A (Artery): Thick muscular walls (smooth muscle layer is well-developed). Narrow lumen to withstand high blood pressure. Carries oxygenated blood (except pulmonary artery) from the heart to tissues. B (Capillary): Smallest blood vessel with thin, single-layered walls (endothelium). Allows exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste between blood and tissues. Forms networks between arteries and veins. C (Vein): Thinner walls compared to arteries, with a wider lumen. Contains valves to prevent backflow of blood. Carries deoxygenated blood (except pulmonary vein) from tissues back to the heart. From the diagram: A has a thick muscular wall and a narrow lumen → Artery. B has a thin wall with small lumen → Capillary. C has a wide lumen and thinner muscular walls → Vein. Thus, the correct answer is A) A–Artery, B–Capillary, C–Vein.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelles as Reason R: Assertion (A): The tunica media is comparatively thin in the veins.Reason (R): Each vein consists of three layers; tunica intima, tunica media, and tunica externa.In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: Veins have a thin tunica media compared to arteries because they carry blood under low pressure. Arteries, in contrast, have a thicker tunica media to withstand the high pressure exerted by the heart. Reason (R) is also true: Veins have three layers: Tunica intima (inner layer) Tunica media (middle layer, smooth muscle) Tunica externa (outer fibrous layer) However, Reason (R) does not directly explain Assertion (A): While veins do have three layers, this fact does not explain why the tunica media is thinner in veins. The actual reason for the thin tunica media in veins is the low-pressure blood flow.

questions.question: Match the List-I and List-II, and choose the correct combination. List-I List-II (A) Tunica externa (P) Mesothelial cells (B) Tunica media (Q) Single layer of epithelial cells (C) Tunica intima (R) Smooth muscles, elastic fibres (D) Epicardium (S) Elastic, collagen fibres
questions.explanation: Tunica externa (A): This is the outermost layer of a blood vessel. It is primarily composed of elastic and collagen fibers. Therefore, A matches with S. Tunica media (B): This is the middle layer of a blood vessel wall. It is mainly made up of smooth muscles and elastic fibers. Therefore, B matches with R. Tunica intima (C): This is the innermost layer of a blood vessel. It is a single layer of epithelial cells (endothelium). Therefore, C matches with Q. Epicardium (D): This is the outermost layer of the heart wall, also known as the visceral pericardium. It is made of mesothelial cells. Therefore, D matches with P.

questions.question: Capillaries are the connection between
questions.explanation: Explanation: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels in the circulatory system. They serve as the site of exchange for gases, nutrients, and waste between blood and tissues. Capillaries connect arterioles (small branches of arteries) to venules (small branches of veins). Why Option C is correct: Arteries → Arterioles → Capillaries → Venules → Veins Capillaries do not directly connect arteries to veins, but rather connect arterioles to venules. Why Other Options Are Incorrect: Option A (Arteries and veins): ❌ Capillaries do not connect directly to arteries and veins. Option B (Veins and arteries): ❌ Incorrect because the order should be arteries → capillaries → veins, not veins to arteries. Option D (None of the above): ❌ Incorrect because capillaries do connect arterioles and venules. Thus, the correct answer is C) Arterioles and venules. ✅

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an artery?
options: Carries blood away from the heart
questions.explanation: Explanation: Arteries are blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to various parts of the body. They transport oxygenated blood in most cases, except for the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. Why Other Options Are Incorrect? Option B (Carries oxygenated blood) ❌ While most arteries carry oxygenated blood, the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood, making this statement not universally true. Option C (Contains valves) ❌ Arteries do not have valves because blood flows under high pressure, unlike veins, which have valves to prevent backflow. Option D (Has thin walls) ❌ Arteries have thick, muscular walls to withstand the high pressure exerted by blood being pumped from the heart. Final Answer: ✅ A) Carries blood away from the heart.

questions.question: A unique vascular connection between the digestive tract and liver is called________.
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal system is a unique vascular connection that transports nutrient-rich blood from the digestive tract to the liver through the hepatic portal vein. This allows the liver to process nutrients, detoxify substances, and regulate metabolism before the blood enters the systemic circulation.

questions.question: Which of the following carries blood rich in food materials, such as glucose and amino acids, from intestine to liver?
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the intestine to the liver. This blood contains absorbed glucose, amino acids, and other nutrients, which the liver processes before distributing them to the rest of the body.

questions.question: The hepatic portal vein drains blood to liver from
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the intestine to the liver. This allows the liver to process absorbed nutrients, detoxify harmful substances, and regulate metabolism before the blood enters systemic circulation.

questions.question: Normal activities of the heart are regulated by_________.
questions.explanation: Explanation:The normal activities of the heart are regulated by nodal tissue, which consists of specialized cardiac muscle fibers that generate and conduct electrical impulses. The main components include: Sinoatrial (SA) node: The natural pacemaker of the heart, initiating rhythmic contractions. Atrioventricular (AV) node: Delays impulses from the SA node before transmitting them to the ventricles. Bundle of His and Purkinje fibers: Conduct impulses to the ventricular muscles, ensuring coordinated contraction. Option A (brain) is incorrect because while the brain (medulla oblongata) modulates heart rate through the autonomic nervous system, the heart’s normal rhythm is controlled by nodal tissue. Option B (spinal cord) is incorrect because the spinal cord does not directly regulate heart activity. Option C (hormones) is incorrect because hormones like adrenaline influence heart rate but do not regulate its normal rhythm. Thus, the correct answer is D) Nodal tissue.

questions.question: Cardiac activity could be moderated by the autonomous neural system. Choose the correct option.
options: The parasympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume.
The sympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume.
The parasympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increase stroke volume.
The sympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increase stroke volume.
questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system (ANS) regulates cardiac activity: The sympathetic system releases noradrenaline, which increases heart rate and stroke volume by enhancing the force of contraction. The parasympathetic system (via the vagus nerve) releases acetylcholine, which reduces heart rate and cardiac output. Thus, the sympathetic system stimulates both heart rate and stroke volume, making option B correct.

questions.question: Neural signal through sympathetic nerves of autonomic nervous system (ANS) can; I. increase the heart beat rate. II. decrease the heart beat rate. III. increase the strength of ventricular contraction. IV. decrease the speed of the conduction of action potential. V. increase cardiac output. VI. decrease cardiac output.
questions.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system (ANS) stimulates the heart by: (I) Increasing the heart rate by releasing noradrenaline. (III) Increasing the strength of ventricular contraction, leading to stronger heartbeats. (V) Increasing cardiac output by enhancing both heart rate and stroke volume. Incorrect statements: (II) Decrease in heart rate is a function of the parasympathetic nervous system, not the sympathetic system. (IV) Decrease in speed of conduction is also incorrect; the sympathetic system increases the speed of action potential conduction. (VI) Decrease in cardiac output contradicts the function of sympathetic stimulation. Thus, the correct answer is D (I, III and V only). [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 293]

questions.question: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Neural signals through sympathetic nerves can increase the strength of ventricular contraction. Reason R: Parasympathetic neural signals synergistically act with sympathetic neural signal to increase the cardiac output. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: The sympathetic nervous system releases noradrenaline, which increases the strength of ventricular contraction, leading to a higher cardiac output. Reason (R) is false: The parasympathetic nervous system does not act synergistically with the sympathetic system to increase cardiac output. Instead, it has an opposite effect by reducing heart rate and cardiac output through the release of acetylcholine. Thus, the correct answer is C.

questions.question: Assertion: Volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle of heart per second is called the cardiac output. Reason: Cardiac output is equal to the product of stroke volume and heart rate (approx 5 litres).
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true, and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true, but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, and Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, and Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: During a cardiac cycle, each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood which is called the stroke volume. The stroke volume multiplied by the heart rate (no. of beats per min.) gives the cardiac output. Therefore, the cardiac output can be defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute and averages 5000 mL or 5 litres in a healthy individual. The body has the ability to alter the stroke volume as well as the heart rate and thereby the cardiac output. For example, the cardiac output of an athlete will be much higher than that of an ordinary man.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true regarding angina?
options: Does not affect the blood flow.
Not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscles.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Angina (angina pectoris) is a condition where insufficient oxygen supply reaches the heart muscles due to reduced blood flow, usually caused by coronary artery disease (CAD). Other options are incorrect: (A) Heart stops beating → This describes cardiac arrest, not angina. (B) More common in children → Angina is more common in adults, especially those with risk factors like hypertension and atherosclerosis. (C) Does not affect blood flow → Angina is caused by restricted blood flow due to narrowed coronary arteries. Thus, the correct answer is (D) Not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscles.

questions.question: The normal blood pressure is _____ and if it gets increased, such a disorder is called ____ .
questions.explanation: Explanation: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic). Hypertension is a condition where blood pressure is persistently higher than normal (typically above 140/90 mmHg). Other options are incorrect: (B) 80/120 is incorrect because systolic pressure is always higher than diastolic. (C) 120/80 with hypotension is incorrect because hypotension refers to low blood pressure (below 90/60 mmHg). (D) 100/60; hypertension is incorrect as 100/60 is low blood pressure (hypotension), not hypertension. Thus, the correct answer is (A) 120/80; hypertension.

questions.question: Which one of following is a incorrect match? Disorders Symptoms 1. Heart failure Insufficient blood supply to the body 2. Angina pectoris Acute chest pain 3. Cardiac arrest Lumen narrows 4. Heart attack Insufficient blood supply to cardiac muscles
questions.explanation: Explanation: Cardiac arrest is a condition where the heart stops beating suddenly due to electrical disturbances. It is not characterized by lumen narrowing. Correct matches: Heart failure → Insufficient blood supply to the body (correct) Angina pectoris → Acute chest pain due to reduced oxygen supply (correct) Heart attack (Myocardial infarction) → Insufficient blood supply to cardiac muscles due to blockage (correct) Thus, the incorrect match is (C) 3 (Cardiac arrest - Lumen narrows).

questions.question: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is also referred as;
questions.explanation: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is also known as atherosclerosis, a condition where plaque builds up inside the coronary arteries, reducing blood flow to the heart. Other options are incorrect: Angina (B) is a symptom of CAD, causing chest pain due to reduced oxygen supply. Heart failure (C) is a condition where the heart fails to pump blood effectively, which may result from CAD but is not the same as CAD. Heart attack (D) (myocardial infarction) is a severe consequence of CAD but not its synonym. Thus, the correct answer is (A) Atherosclerosis.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Heart failure is the same as cardiac arrest.
Angina is not common in middle age and elderly.
High blood pressure is 120/80 mm of Hg.
Cardiac arrest is when the heart stops beating.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Cardiac arrest is a condition where the heart stops beating suddenly due to electrical disturbances, leading to loss of consciousness and circulation failure. Other options are incorrect: (A) Heart failure is the same as cardiac arrest → Incorrect. Heart failure is a chronic condition where the heart is unable to pump blood effectively, while cardiac arrest is a sudden event. (B) Angina is not common in middle age and elderly → Incorrect. Angina is more common in middle-aged and elderly individuals due to coronary artery disease. (C) High blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg → Incorrect. 120/80 mmHg is normal blood pressure, while hypertension is typically above 140/90 mmHg. Thus, the correct answer is (D) Cardiac arrest is when the heart stops beating.

questions.question: Statement-I: 190/110 mm Hg blood pressure may harm vital organs like brain and kidneys. Statement-II: Repeated 140/90 mm Hg blood pressure is considered as hypertension and requires treatment.
options: Statement I and Statement II both are correct.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Statement I and Statement II both are incorrect.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Statement I is correct: A blood pressure of 190/110 mmHg is considered severe hypertension, which can damage vital organs like the brain and kidneys, leading to complications such as stroke, kidney failure, and heart attack. Statement II is correct: A persistent blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or higher is classified as hypertension and requires lifestyle modifications and medical treatment to prevent complications. Since both statements are correct, the correct answer is (A) Statement I and Statement II both are correct.

questions.question: Systolic blood pressure of a patient is 140 mm Hg while his diastolic blood pressure is 90 mm Hg. If this is not controlled, it can lead to; (I) heart disease. (II) brain haemorrhage. (III) damage of the blood vessels of kidney
questions.explanation: Explanation: A blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg is classified as hypertension, which, if uncontrolled, can lead to: Heart disease (I) – High blood pressure increases the workload on the heart, leading to coronary artery disease (CAD), heart failure, or heart attacks. Brain hemorrhage (II) – Hypertension can weaken blood vessels in the brain, increasing the risk of stroke or brain hemorrhage. Damage to blood vessels of the kidney (III) – High blood pressure can damage the glomeruli and small blood vessels in the kidneys, leading to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Since all three complications can occur due to uncontrolled hypertension, the correct answer is (D) All of these.

questions.question: Statement I: Heart failure is sometimes called congestive heart failure. Statement II: Congestion of the lungs is one the main symptoms of heart failure.
options: Statement I and Statement II both are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I and Statement II both are incorrect.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Statement I is correct: Heart failure is often referred to as congestive heart failure (CHF) because it leads to the accumulation of fluid (congestion) in the lungs, liver, and other tissues due to inefficient pumping by the heart. Statement II is correct: Lung congestion (pulmonary edema) is one of the main symptoms of heart failure, particularly left-sided heart failure, where blood backs up into the lungs, causing shortness of breath and fluid buildup. Since both statements are correct, the correct answer is (A) Statement I and Statement II both are correct.
